newsitem.title: FRANCE: Volvo Car to launch marketing offensive.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Car to launch marketing offensive.

text.p: Volvo Cars will launch a marketing offensive in the fourth quarter to reconquer lost market share in Europe, the president of Europe Marketing of Volvo Cars, Hans-Olov Olsson, told Reuters on Tuesday.

"We will launch a massive marketing offensive in Europe in the fourth quarter of this year. Our strategy now is to work according to a quarter-by-quarter attack scheme. Our top priority is to secure deliveries and their dependability," Olsson said in an interview.
Volvo Cars will also focus on customer relations and is urging dealers to seek out potential new customers.
"Our delivery problems with the S40/V40 turned customers away, but now those problems of course also cover the 850- ad 900-series," Olsson said.
The marketing offensive will also include customer financing schemes.
Future plans include an expansion of sales to people younger than the typical Volvo buyer through the launch of special variants of the 850 series, but also through the S40/V40.

"The S40/V40 will be further developed till the year 2000. Furthermore we will add new things to our product line, for example a new generation of stationwagons. We will also raise our presence in the top of the line segment," Olsson said.

By the year 2000, Volvo Cars will use two distinct platforms for their S- and V-lines (sedan and versatility). The C-line (coupe and convertible) will stay a niche product to complement to mainstream models.
"Our S- and V-lines will offer products to cover the entire segment from pre-family to family and post-family," Olsson said.
In the next century sales will shift somewhat and Olsson sees 50 percent of sales in Europe and 25 percent each in North America and Southeast Asia/Japan.
"These three areas will be the major markets that we will focus on," Olsson said.
